items.title: 3.4.1 Formation of sigma and pi bonds

source_refs.note: Topic 3.4.1 with the following pi bond section, printed pages 59-61 (Figures 3.22 to 3.26), with Quick Check 3.7 as the self-check.

blocks.text: A sigma bond is formed by the linear overlap of two half-filled atomic orbitals on adjacent atoms; the orbitals approach each other on the nuclear axis. Both s and p orbitals can overlap head-on to form sigma bonds.

items: s-s overlap: the s orbital of one atom overlaps the s orbital of the other to give a bond orbital. This happens in the formation of H2, where each hydrogen atom has a half-filled s orbital; after bonding the electrons are paired and the electron density is symmetrical around the two nuclei.

s-p overlap: the s orbital of one atom overlaps a p orbital of the other to form a sigma bond. In HCl a half-filled s orbital of hydrogen overlaps a half-filled p orbital of chlorine; the electron density is higher close to the chlorine atom because of its higher electronegativity, which is why HCl is a polar molecule.
p-p overlap: in Cl2 the p orbitals of two chlorine atoms overlap on the nuclear axis; the electron density is symmetrical around the two nuclei because both atoms have the same electronegativity.

blocks.text: The H2S molecule is non-linear. Two 3p orbitals of sulfur (say 3py and 3pz), each with one electron, overlap the 1s orbitals of two hydrogen atoms, forming a v-shaped molecule with a bond angle of 92 degrees. The bond angle in H2O is 104.5 degrees whereas in H2S it is 92 degrees, because the orbitals of sulfur are larger and the lone pair exerts a stronger repulsion.

Consider the double bond between oxygen atoms, O=O. Each atom has two unpaired electrons in perpendicular p orbitals, say px and py. The px orbitals of the two atoms overlap end to end, linearly, and give a sigma bond. The py orbitals are aligned parallel to each other and overlap sideways, two lobes above the plane of the nuclei and two below; this forms a pi bond. The oxygen atoms are doubly bonded through a sigma and a pi bond.

blocks.alt: Top: three overlap pictures, two spheres merging for H2, a sphere meeting a p lobe for HCl with the density shifted to chlorine, and two p lobes meeting end to end for Cl2. Bottom left: sulfur with two p orbitals at right angles bonding two hydrogens at 92 degrees. Bottom right: two oxygen atoms with px lobes overlapping on the axis for the sigma bond and parallel py lobes overlapping above and below for the pi bond.
blocks.caption: Sigma bonds by s-s, s-p and p-p overlap, the H2S angle, and the sigma plus pi double bond of O2 (original diagram after Figures 3.22 to 3.26).
blocks.long_description: A sigma bond is a head-on overlap on the line joining the nuclei: s with s in H2, s with p in HCl, p with p in Cl2. In HCl the density sits nearer chlorine, so the bond is polar; in H2 and Cl2 it is symmetrical. In H2S the two half-filled 3p orbitals of sulfur are at right angles, so the bonds meet at 92 degrees. In O2 the px orbitals overlap end to end for the sigma bond and the parallel py orbitals overlap sideways for the pi bond, giving the double bond.

blocks.prompt: Draw in words the orbital structures of H2O and N2, and the overlaps that form F2 and HF.
blocks.explanation: H2O: two half-filled 2p orbitals of oxygen overlap the 1s orbitals of two hydrogen atoms, two s-p sigma bonds; the two lone pairs push the angle to 104.5 degrees. N2: each nitrogen has three unpaired 2p electrons; one pair of p orbitals overlaps end to end for a sigma bond and the other two pairs overlap sideways for two pi bonds, a triple bond. F2: a half-filled 2p orbital of each fluorine overlaps head-on, a p-p sigma bond, symmetrical. HF: hydrogen's 1s overlaps fluorine's half-filled 2p, an s-p sigma bond with density shifted to fluorine, so HF is polar.

items: Sigma bond: linear overlap on the nuclear axis, s-s (H2), s-p (HCl, polar), p-p (Cl2). H2S: two perpendicular 3p orbitals of S give a 92 degree angle (H2O 104.5).
Pi bond: sideways overlap of parallel p orbitals above and below the axis; O=O is one sigma plus one pi bond.
